transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?
Hello... I'm a little embarrassed to be here, but I keep trying to get rid of what I eat after I overdo it. It's gotten to the point where I feel like I just can't stop doing it on my own.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'getting rid of what you eat' - are you using methods like vomiting, laxatives, or something else?

Yes, I make myself throw up. I go into the bathroom and turn the fan on so my husband can't hear me, because I feel so incredibly ashamed. It just feels like the only way to erase what I've eaten and calm the panic about the calories, even though I feel so guilty afterward.
How often do you find yourself engaging in these episodes of eating followed by purging, and has this behavior been occurring regularly over the past few months?

This cycle has been going on for about seven months now, ever since my husband's heart condition got worse and my doctor started pushing me about my weight. It happens about once or twice a week, usually on the days when caregiving has been especially exhausting and stressful.

Can you describe what happens during these episodes of eating before you purge - do you feel like you're eating a large amount of food in a short time, and is it accompanied by a sense of loss of control?

Yes, it really feels like a switch flips and I start eating almost in a trance, unable to stop even when I want to. I'll stand in the kitchen and go through a huge amount of food in one sitting, like half a pan of brownies, dinner rolls, and leftovers. I keep eating way past the point of being comfortably full, and my hands just keep reaching for more.

During these episodes of eating large amounts of food, do you always feel a sense of loss of control, or are there times when you feel like you're eating this way for reasons other than feeling out of control?

Yes, it always feels like a complete loss of control once it starts. It's like a switch flips where I tell myself to stop, but my hands just keep reaching for more food in a sort of trance until I'm uncomfortably stuffed.
Have you ever had episodes where you ate a large amount of food in a short time without feeling the need to purge afterwards?

No, I almost always feel an overwhelming need to purge after those large eating episodes. The panic about the calories and the intense guilt are so strong that I feel forced to throw up to "erase" what I just did. It has basically become an automatic part of the cycle whenever I overeat like that.

Can you estimate how many times a month you have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short time, followed by purging, versus episodes where you might eat a large amount but don't purge afterwards, if that ever happens?

It happens about four to eight times a month, usually on those stressful days when I'm exhausted from taking care of my husband. I almost never have one of those large eating episodes without throwing up afterward, because the panic and urge to "undo" what I ate is just too strong to resist.
Have you ever experienced episodes of eating large amounts of food in a short time without feeling the need to purge afterwards, or is purging always part of your response to overeating?

Yes, purging is almost always my response to those large eating episodes. The panic and shame about the calories afterward are so overwhelming that forcing myself to throw up feels like the only way to "erase" what I just did and calm down.
Have you ever used other methods to purge, such as laxatives or diuretics, in addition to self-induced vomiting?
No, I've never used laxatives or water pills or anything like that. I only make myself throw up to get rid of the food, even though I'm deeply ashamed to admit it.
Can you recall any instances where you ate a large amount of food in a short time and didn't feel the need to purge afterwards, even if it was just once or very rarely?

I really can't recall any times like that. Whenever I have one of those large eating episodes, the panic and guilt about the calories always kick in immediately, making me feel like I absolutely have to get rid of it.
